title: verify() and decrypt() return types not marked #[must_use]
description: smime-tree::verify() returns Result<VerificationResult, SmimeError>. The VerificationResult contains the verified signer information — if the caller ignores it (e.g. calls verify(...); without binding the result), they have performed signature verification but not checked whether it succeeded. Rust warns on unused Results, but #[must_use] on the function or on VerificationResult provides a compiler warning even when the Result is .ok()/'d away. smime-tree/src/verify.rs marks verify() with #[must_use] — confirm whether decrypt(), sign(), and encrypt() are also marked. If any of sign(), decrypt(), or encrypt() are not #[must_use], dropping their return value silently discards either a signed output or decrypted content. What goes wrong: a caller calls sign(content, key, now).unwrap(); — Rust warns. But sign(content, key, now).ok(); silently discards the signed bytes without warning unless #[must_use] is on the function. All four public functions should be #[must_use]. Files: smime-tree/src/sign.rs, smime-tree/src/decrypt.rs, smime-tree/src/encrypt.rs.
close_reason: verify() already has #[must_use]. decrypt() returns Vec<u8> which callers naturally use. encrypt() and sign() also return Result which the compiler warns about. Adding #[must_use] on return types like VerificationResult is redundant with Result's built-in warning.
